conversion_metric: Operating cash flow as percent of gross rental capex
calculation_or_source: 3.305B USD operating cash flow / 2.931B USD gross rental capex
what_it_proves: URI generated more operating cash flow than gross rental capex during H1 2026, so the fleet-capital program was not being funded only by external capital in that window.
what_it_does_not_prove: This does not prove marginal fleet returns, asset-class utilization, or exact funding source for each equipment purchase.
next_source: Filed cash-flow statement, debt note, ABL/securitization availability, and fleet category mix.

calculation_or_source: 2.720B USD rental-equipment cash purchases - 680M USD rental-equipment sale proceeds
what_it_proves: URI's H1 fleet cash commitment is smaller after used-equipment recycling, which is central to the fleet-access model.
what_it_does_not_prove: Net cash investment does not prove the quality of the sold fleet, gain/loss on sales, or replacement economics.
next_source: Used-equipment sales margin, fleet age by class, and disposal proceeds recovery.

conversion_metric: Rental revenue as percent of OEC
calculation_or_source: 3.849B USD Q2 rental revenue / 23.8B USD OEC
what_it_proves: URI's rental fleet generated quarterly rental revenue equal to about 16.2% of OEC, giving a simple revenue/OEC productivity proxy.
what_it_does_not_prove: This is not ROIC, utilization, margin, or time utilization; OEC is replacement cost and rental revenue includes owned, re-rent, and ancillary revenue.
next_source: OEC by segment, owned equipment rental revenue, rental gross margin, time utilization, rate, and mix.

calculation_or_source: 23.8B USD Q2 2026 OEC - 22.48B USD FY2025 OEC
what_it_proves: URI's fleet scale increased by about 1.32B USD, or 5.9%, from year-end 2025 to Q2 2026, consistent with active fleet-capital deployment.
what_it_does_not_prove: OEC growth can come from price, mix, acquisition, and replacement effects; it is not pure organic capacity growth.
next_source: OEC roll-forward by purchase, acquisition, sale, depreciation proxy, category, and region.

calculation_or_source: Company disclosure; footnote says fleet productivity reflects rental rates, time utilization, and mix on owned equipment rental revenue.
what_it_proves: URI's own definition makes fleet productivity the right conversion bridge from fleet dollars to operating output.
what_it_does_not_prove: The metric is aggregated and does not tell us which asset classes, geographies, or customer segments drove the increase.
next_source: Pull fleet productivity bridge components and segment/category disclosures.

conversion_metric: Gross rental capex guide midpoint increase
calculation_or_source: Current gross purchases guide midpoint 5.05B USD versus prior midpoint 4.6B USD
what_it_proves: URI raised its 2026 gross fleet-purchase program and had already deployed heavy H1 fleet capex, indicating ongoing capital absorption rather than a completed 2025 cycle.
what_it_does_not_prove: Guidance is not a completed spend figure and could include replacement, inflation, mix, or demand timing.
next_source: Track later 2026 filings for actual gross purchases, net capex, OEC, productivity, and free cash flow.

calculation_or_source: Company disclosure; liquidity includes cash plus ABL and accounts receivable securitization facility availability.
what_it_proves: URI's fleet investment sits next to explicit liquidity channels, including ABL and accounts receivable securitization capacity.
what_it_does_not_prove: Liquidity is not use-of-proceeds proof and does not identify which facility funded which fleet purchases.
next_source: Extract URI facility table, borrowing base, maturities, pricing, collateral, and AR securitization capacity.

conversion_metric: Acquisition revenue contribution as percent of revenue
calculation_or_source: 250.8M USD acquisition revenue contribution / 1.168B USD Q2 revenue
what_it_proves: A material share of Sterling's Q2 growth came from acquired revenue, so the pass separates acquisition-enabled capability from organic demand.
what_it_does_not_prove: This does not disprove organic growth; it prevents treating all reported growth as same-store data-center/mission-critical demand.
next_source: Pull segment revenue excluding CEC and Stone Ridge and pro forma acquisition tables.

calculation_or_source: 5.62B USD combined backlog / 1.168B USD Q2 revenue
what_it_proves: Sterling's backlog funnel is large relative to current quarterly revenue, supporting the visibility claim.
what_it_does_not_prove: Combined backlog includes unsigned awards and is not guaranteed revenue, cash, or margin.
next_source: Separate RPOs, MSAs, unsigned awards, future phases, and conversion timing.

conversion_metric: Combined backlog to 2026 revenue guide midpoint
calculation_or_source: 5.62B USD combined backlog / 4.08B USD 2026 revenue guide midpoint
what_it_proves: Sterling's combined backlog exceeds a full-year revenue-guide midpoint, reinforcing field-execution visibility.
what_it_does_not_prove: This comparison mixes backlog and guidance; it does not prove duration, margin, or signed/funded status.
next_source: Backlog aging, expected revenue-recognition schedule, and signed backlog conversion.

conversion_metric: CEC and Stone Ridge contribution to signed backlog plus unsigned awards
calculation_or_source: 1.32B USD signed backlog contribution + 1.24B USD unsigned-awards contribution
what_it_proves: Sterling's acquisition contribution to the backlog funnel is very large, about 45.6% of Q2 combined backlog, so acquisition capital is part of the capital-flow mechanism.
what_it_does_not_prove: The acquisition contribution does not identify organic project demand or prove acquired backlog quality.
next_source: Build organic/acquired backlog bridge and track conversion over the next quarters.

calculation_or_source: 328.021M USD operating cash flow - 69.646M USD capital expenditures
what_it_proves: Sterling generated substantial cash in excess of company capex, consistent with an execution platform rather than a balance-sheet-heavy fleet owner.
what_it_does_not_prove: This is not project-level free cash flow and does not show whether contract assets or billings will reverse favorably.
next_source: Contract assets/liabilities, costs in excess of billings, billings in excess, and project-reserve movement.

calculation_or_source: 1.5B USD expanded revolving credit facility / 150M USD prior revolver capacity
what_it_proves: Sterling materially expanded company-level liquidity for platform growth and used proceeds to repay the existing term loan.
what_it_does_not_prove: This is company funding capacity, not customer project financing or return proof.
next_source: Credit agreement, covenant package, pricing, maturity, and acquisition-use language.

conversion_metric: Unsigned awards as percent of combined backlog
calculation_or_source: 1.28B USD unsigned awards / 5.62B USD combined backlog
what_it_proves: About 22.8% of combined backlog is unsigned awards, so the page can explicitly separate committed work from weaker visibility.
what_it_does_not_prove: Unsigned awards are pending contract execution and should not be counted as signed backlog.
next_source: Award letters, final contract execution, cancellation/modification, and conversion schedule.

conversion_metric: Future-phase opportunities as percent of visibility to future work
calculation_or_source: 1.4B USD future-phase opportunities / greater-than-7.0B USD visibility to future work; approximate lower-bound share
what_it_proves: Future phases are a meaningful but lower-confidence part of Sterling's work funnel and should be described as optionality on active sites, not backlog.
what_it_does_not_prove: The denominator is a greater-than value, so the percentage is approximate and should not be treated as exact.
next_source: Track future-phase awards, contract execution, and revenue conversion.

calculation_or_source: Backlog is large and cash conversion is positive, but acquisition and unsigned/future-phase buckets remain material.
what_it_proves: Sterling has first-pass conversion support, but the correct status is bounded: cash conversion exists, backlog visibility is high, and acquisition/unsigned/future buckets must be kept separate.
what_it_does_not_prove: It does not yet prove fully funded backlog, customer economics, organic growth quality, or project-level returns.
next_source: Contract assets/liabilities and backlog roll-forward conversion pass.
